issues.problem: The r1 recall repair returns False for any ambiguous name followed by a subject verb, before the Title-Case-compound and role-connector checks run. It also exempts every capitalised '-ly' word. That reopens the r4-2 false-positive class for the commonest sentence shape, a compound noun as subject. The r4 set stays 0/14 only because none of its sentences has a verb right after the name. Example: 'Netflix Conductor and Temporal are ...' passes, but 'Netflix Conductor orchestrates ...' fails. The false credits reach classifier evidence and prose-vote targets for any run whose sources discuss workflow engines, design patterns or job titles. They do not reach the real APO run (classification and cells unchanged).

issues.suggested_fix: Do not let the subject-verb test override the compound or role checks. Accept a capitalised previous word only when '<Prev> <Name>' is itself a known display name or alias, or the previous word is a known maker of that product (e.g. derived from pack parentheticals such as 'Conductor (Melty Labs)'). Restrict the '-ly' exemption to a previous word that is itself sentence-initial ('Notably Director ...'). Add the fp2 sentences above to STILL_PLAIN_ENGLISH.

issues.suggested_fix: Also start a clause at ', but|, while|, whereas|, though|, yet', '(', ' - ', ' — ' and ':'. Alternatively, blank only the span from the nearest vendor mention before the marker, so the clause is bounded by the vendor the marker is about.

issues.problem: These are precision losses against prev, back to orig behaviour. Negation of a vendor's own claim in a following clause or sentence no longer vetoes it, and neither does 'without' or 'missing evidence', which were dropped from the marker. _GATE_VERB has no word end ('block\w*'), so 'blockchain' counts as a gate verb. A gate verb anywhere earlier in the clause also exempts it ('Reviewers rejected the claim that ...: no evidence'). No such cell on the real run.

No public evidence supports it.', 'Deepwork markets workflow composition, missing evidence.', 'Deepwork provides workflow composition, and zero independent evidence exists.', 'Reviewers rejected the claim that Deepwork provides workflow composition: no evidence.' and 'Deepwork, built on a blockchain ledger, provides workflow composition with no evidence.'
issues.suggested_fix: Bound _GATE_VERB with \b and an explicit suffix list (block(s|ed|ing)?, refus(e|es|ed|ing), ...). Require the gate verb to govern the marker (within a few words before it). When the absence clause has no vendor of its own ('there is no public evidence for this', 'No public evidence supports it'), apply it to the vendor of the previous clause. Restore 'without|missing (public|independent)? evidence' except after a gate verb.

issues.problem: The 'hard exclusion' marker blanks its whole clause, including a genuine positive about an in-scope vendor that merely mentions the hard-exclusion list.
issues.evidence: absence2.py: 'Silver Bullet provides hook-enforced gates and is not on the hard-exclusion list.' and 'Unlike the hard exclusions, Silver Bullet provides workflow composition.' tick at orig and prev, but give {} at head. 'Director, which is not a hard exclusion, provides workflow composition.' gives {} at every version. 'Hard exclusions: Sweep, Windsurf. Silver Bullet provides ...' is fine.
issues.suggested_fix: Only drop the votes of the vendors listed after the hard-exclusion marker (up to the clause end), or skip when the marker is negated ('not (on )?(a|the) hard-exclusion'). Add the two sentences as keep cases.

issues.problem: Opener words that are now function words (Next, First, Finally, Plus, Today) make the following name non-sentence-initial, so it counts with no further check. A cue word after the name bypasses the compound check entirely. Mostly contrived.
issues.evidence: fp2.py head (and the mutant): 'Next Continue with the setup wizard.' -> continue, 'Finally Sweep the floor ...' -> sweep, 'First Linear then quadratic ...' -> linear, 'Plus Director approval is needed.' and 'Today Director-level approval ...' -> director, 'The Abstract Factory Plus pattern ...' and 'The Agentic Software Factory Enterprise tier ...' -> factory-ai.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat a name whose previous word is a sentence-initial function word as sentence-initial (subject or possessive required). Check the prev-word compound before accepting a cue.

issues.problem: Nit. The scope check is a prefix test on the first line, so a multi-line previous query whose first line equals the new query is taken as the same query, and its auto profile (category = old multi-line topic) is carried. A recorded manifest query that differs does not stop the scope fallback.
issues.suggested_fix: When the manifest records a query, decide on it alone. Otherwise compare the full topic line through the next 'Research type:' line, or the whole generated header.
